text:
Dante Miller: FYI  Had to take a taxi from Paddington -> City yesterday because of the tube strike. Taxi charged 48.60 GBP, I paid on personal card because corp card declined at the reader. Receipt from QuickCar UK shows total and driver id but no VAT number. Two questions: 1) is VAT reclaimable without a vendor VAT number? 2) our taxi cap is 40 GBP/day  any chance of exception for strike-related overage?
expense-bot: Reminder: attach original merchant receipt + bank/cc statement showing charge + manager approval for any exceptions. Policy: https://intra.redwood/finance/expenses#transport-caps
Lena (Finance Ops): Short answers: 1) Without a VAT invoice or supplier VAT number we typically can't reclaim VAT. If the vendor can provide an invoice later with VAT registration we can amend. 2) Overage: normally subject to manager approval as an exception. Please upload the receipt, bank statement, and get manager sign-off. If approved, we'll reimburse the full gross amount but tag the portion as non-reclaimable VAT if no VAT id.
Dante Miller: uploading receipt and my card statement now. I pinged Vik for approval.
Vik Patel: Approved. Given the tube strike and safety concerns, exception approved for full fare. Mark as manager-exception.
Lena (Finance Ops): Thanks Vik. Processing reimbursement: 48.60 GBP. Using daily FX 1 GBP = 1.25 USD -> USD 60.75. Reimbursement will appear in USD on payroll payout. Note: VAT flagged non-reclaimable until vendor supplies VAT number. Tagging expense: travel:transport, label: manager-exception, tax: non-reclaimable.
Emma (Travel Ops): For future strikes we can add a one-off guidance note on travel page about pre-approvals for same-day disruptions. Happy to draft a short blurb.
Dante Miller: great, thanks all. Quick follow-up  should I ask QuickCar for VAT invoice or just note it?
Lena (Finance Ops): Ask them. If they provide a VAT invoice we can retroactively claim. Please forward any update to finance@redwood.
Dante Miller: will do :thumbsup:
